newsitem.title: CANADA: TransAlta acquires remainder of AEC Power.
newsitem.headline: TransAlta acquires remainder of AEC Power.

text.p: TransAlta Corp unit TransAlta Energy Corp said on Wednesday it acquired another two-thirds interest in AEC Power Ltd, which operates Syncrude Canada Ltd 's utilities plant, from Alberta Energy Co Ltd.
The move gave TransAlta full ownership of the company.
AEC Power owns the facility that supplies electricity and steam to the oil sands mining and synthetic oil producer in northern Alberta.
TransAlta said it paid Alberta Energy C$32.6 million to acquire AEC Power's remaining shares and C$66.7 million to assume and retire its outstanding debt.

"TransAlta Energy is well-positioned to pursue future business opportunities with the Syncrude project and other industrial concerns," Alan Moon, TransAlta Energy president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
The 260 MW plant is Canada's largest cogeneration facility and has been in service since 1978, when Syncrude began operations.
AEC president and chief executive Gwyn Morgan said the sale of AEC power was the last of its non-core asset sales.
Morgan said AEC would continue its role in Syncrude through its 13.75-percent ownership interest.

The company, which has been divesting non-core assets for four years, now concentrates entirely on oil and gas exploration and production, non-utility pipelines, gas storage and processing, he said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
